content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The image has pixel rulers along its top and left edges (x increases to the right, y increases downward, 0 at the image's top-left corner). Using the ruler scale, give the position of a point inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: (x, y)

This axial slice shows a large limb, probably the thigh, with the femur as the dark round structure at about (405, 455). The very bright lobulated structure posterior to it, at about (420, 590), looks like a different tissue, possibly a fluid-filled or fatty region. The tumor is a fibrous lesion, so it should be intermediate to dark on T2.

The large intermediate-to-dark region in the anterior part of the limb spans roughly x 220–490 and y 110–330. It is homogeneous and low in signal, which fits a fibrous tumor such as a desmoid. I estimate its centre at about (350, 220).

ANSWER: (350, 220)
